title: Claude Code Makes Auto Mode the Default on August 14
caption:
On August 14, Claude Code stops asking before it runs things.

Auto mode becomes the default permission mode for new sessions on Pro, Max and Team. It isn't bypass. A classifier screens every action, and it still refuses curl | bash, force pushes, prod deploys, and any push that would carry a secret out of the repo.

I flipped mine to auto weeks ago and haven't looked back. What actually reassured me: a repo's .claude/settings.json can't turn auto on. Only your user settings can.

Manual or auto?

slides.headline:
August 14:
Claude stops asking
slides.sub: Auto mode becomes the default permission mode for new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans. A classifier screens each action instead of prompting you.

slides.title: Auto mode still refuses
items: curl | bash, and anything that downloads then executes
Force push, production deploys, database migrations
Mass deletion on cloud storage, IAM or repo permission grants
Any commit or push that would carry a secret out of the repo

slides.title: Your default stays
slides.sub: Set defaultMode yourself and the switch skips you. Only ~/.claude/settings.json counts, so a repo can't grant itself auto mode.

slides.headline: Check your settings.json
slides.sub: and I'll send the mode breakdown
